how_to_use: Before planning a new implementation, query this index (node tools/reuse.mjs <words>). A capability listed here was researched or catalogued at the commits shown; a missing capability means research first.
guardrails: Spatial IDE's core is AGPL-3.0-or-later: every candidate states its licence and licence class.
Code with no licence, an unverified licence or an incompatible one (classes red, likely-incompatible) is reference only: never ADOPT, WRAP, VENDOR, FORK or PORT. The builder enforces this.
Adopting anything as a new dependency stays the human's typed word: such candidates carry dependency = 'new — the human's typed word'.
Ported code needs a route into the shipped NOTICE before it lands (licence_watch: shell-port-notice-route).

license_classes.permissive: MIT, BSD, Apache-2.0, ISC, Zlib, BSL-1.0 (Boost), public-domain code — notices owed
license_classes.core-combinable-copyleft: GPL-3.0, GPL-2.0-or-later, AGPL-3.0 — usually combinable into the AGPL core; never in an Apache-2.0 SDK or anything a proprietary plugin links
license_classes.weak-copyleft: LGPL, MPL-2.0, EPL — obligations stated in the entry
license_classes.red: SSPL, BSL (Business Source), Elastic, Commons Clause, PolyForm, non-commercial, source-available, no or unverified licence
license_classes.data: dataset licences (ODbL, CDLA, CC, public domain, unidentified) — see the entry's note
license_classes.spec: a specification or standard to follow; no code reused

modes.WRAP: use behind an abstraction Spatial IDE owns
modes.VENDOR: copy a small stable subset with provenance
modes.BENCHMARK: use as a performance or correctness reference

capabilities.title: Open a file only if it resolves inside the project folder, with no gap between the check and the open
capabilities.summary: ADR-036 §5 as drafted (resolve, then open if inside) is the racy pattern. Race-free designs open one segment at a time relative to held directory handles and never follow a link silently; on Windows that is NtCreateFile relative to the parent handle with no-follow. Own the one-operation resolver; borrow the algorithm and the escape-test tables rather than inventing them.

candidates.name: cap-std
candidates.license: Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception OR Apache-2.0 OR MIT
candidates.note: Per-segment resolution beneath a directory handle on Windows and Unix; refuses absolute link targets, so every Windows junction is refused; ~9 crates if taken as a dependency instead.

candidates.name: Go
candidates.note: os.Root (Go 1.24+): same model, public escape history (three Root escape fixes since 2025); its tests are a ready escape table.

candidates.name: Rust std
candidates.note: The CVE-2022-21658 remove_dir_all fix as symlink-race prior art.

candidates.name: fs_at
candidates.note: Openat-style API for Rust including Windows; young.

candidates.name: libpathrs
candidates.note: Linux-only safe path resolution; weak copyleft.

candidates.name: filepath-securejoin
candidates.note: Lexical join plus Linux-only re-checks; not race-free on Windows.

decisions_for_human: Link rule: follow relative links that stay inside the folder, or refuse every link (every junction is absolute, so 'follow' still refuses junctions).
Whether OneDrive placeholders (reparse points) are refused — untested; test on the reference machine.
Ported code needs a route into the shipped NOTICE (see licence_watch: shell-port-notice-route).

capabilities.title: Keep the file the engine opens the same file that the resolver checked
capabilities.summary: DuckDB re-opens data by path (CreateFileW with full sharing), so a contained handle alone does not protect it. Two candidate bridges: hold every handle in the chain without delete-sharing while DuckDB reads (inference from Windows sharing rules, untested), or compare file identity (volume serial plus file ID) before and after, within the session.

decisions_for_human: Which bridge piece 1c's form states: pinned handles or an identity comparison.

capabilities.summary: Refuse reserved device names and trailing-dot/space segments in the canonical text form, not only in the resolver. ADR-036's 'one spelling on every operating system' is overstated: case-insensitivity, 8.3 short names and macOS Unicode decomposition still alias.

capabilities.title: Replace a file atomically at Save (write new, flush, rename over the old)
capabilities.summary: Use std::fs::rename (MoveFileExW REPLACE_EXISTING first, FileRenameInfoEx POSIX fallback on access denied) after sync_all, with a bounded retry on sharing violations. Not ReplaceFileW; not MOVEFILE_WRITE_THROUGH as a durability measure. tempfile's persist does no sync. No project read flushes a directory on Windows. Own a ~60-line helper (inference).

capabilities.summary: 'A final line without LF' is not a sufficient torn-write detector: after power loss a line can end in LF and still hold NUL bytes. Keep the longest prefix of lines that end in LF, contain no NUL, parse, and chain through `parent`; stop at the first failure.

capabilities.title: Open a project by double-clicking its file, on Windows, macOS and Linux

Windows and macOS type a file by its last extension, so `project.spatial.json` is still `.json` (inference from Wine's code and Apple's docs). Recommendation: a fixed single-segment name, Godot-style (`project.godot`), content still canonical JSON. Tauri ships no Linux MIME glob; add one.

capabilities.title: Keep a project's identity across a move, and give a copy a new one
capabilities.summary: Godot 4.4+ uses ADR-036's rule: if the old path still exists the newcomer gets a new ID, if it is gone it is a move; when it cannot tell, it only warns. Always re-key the newly opened folder, and re-read the identity in the old folder rather than only checking it exists. VS Code is the counter-example: path-derived IDs lose state on copy or move.

candidates.note: Counter-example; the reverse-pointer file idea only.

capabilities.title: Collapse repeated edits and cancel toggles when compacting a step history
capabilities.summary: Qt merges only adjacent commands with the same id, never across the clean index, and drops a merge that ends where it started. QGIS adds a same-target check. So the key is (action, property, target); never merge across `saved-here`; an unknown action is opaque, never merged, and ends a run.

capabilities.summary: nbformat keeps cells from a newer version through one open slot. In ADR-036 terms only `intent.params` of an unregistered action under a newer `actions` header is opaque; that step is kept byte for byte on rewrite and never merged; everything else stays closed. Excalidraw, which drops unknown element types, is the counter-example.

capabilities.title: Read canonical JSON strictly: refuse unknown and duplicate keys, bound every member
capabilities.summary: spatial_renderer::canonical only writes. Every reader today parses through serde_json::Value, which silently keeps the last of duplicate keys (verified, 1.0.151). Derived structs with deny_unknown_fields cover struct members; map-shaped members and the byte round-trip need an owned reader half. Decide serde_json's float_roundtrip before relying on a byte round-trip (inferred from source).

capabilities.title: Choose which simplified tier a viewport draws
capabilities.summary: In an orthographic view scale is uniform, so one tier serves the viewport. With a tier key in source units², draw the coarsest tier whose area × 4^zoom ≤ τ px² (fixed zoom thresholds ~1.66 and ~1.16 levels apart — arithmetic, not a measurement; τ must be declared). geo's VW simplifier does not keep areas monotonic, so τ does not bound visual drift — measure it. The pick anchor is read from resident geometry, so it must route to tier 0 by stable id or be pinned by a test.

capabilities.title: Stop the drawn tier flapping on small zooms

capabilities.title: What to draw while a finer tier is still loading
capabilities.summary: Use deck.gl's vocabulary (best-available / no-overlap / never) per tile and tier, plus MapLibre's rule that the coarser tile stays until the finer tile's content is complete. Consequences: lod.tier_resident names several tiers; both count against the vertex budget during a swap; a new 'replaced by a different tier' supersede reason.

capabilities.title: Glyph atlases and GPU text rendering
capabilities.summary: glyphon = cosmic-text + etagere atlas + wgpu. deck.gl's TextLayer uses a TinySDF atlas today.

capabilities.title: A native wgpu renderer for 2D vector maps
capabilities.summary: The bake-off is filed and unscheduled; a label-pipeline spike must precede any renderer-replacement decision. Galileo is an architecture reference only (last release 2025-07, ubuntu-only CI).

candidates.name: galileo
candidates.note: Whole Rust geo renderer; no label collision.

capabilities.title: Coordinate transformations, grids and the EPSG database
capabilities.summary: Once reprojection is scheduled, PROJ via the `proj` crate matches docs/05's vocabulary (pipelines, grids, database versions, PROJJSON). proj4rs does not fit. PROJ's proj.db embeds EPSG v13.104, widening the EPSG-terms question to the whole dataset. Geodesics are already in the tree via geo.

candidates.name: PROJ via `proj` crate
candidates.note: Candidate at the first reprojection; native dependency.

candidates.name: proj4rs
candidates.note: Proj strings only; no WKT/PROJJSON; no LICENSE file.

decisions_for_human: The EPSG dataset terms if proj.db ships.

capabilities.title: Read rasters, COGs and chunked arrays
capabilities.summary: No PLAN node schedules raster. async-tiff is the first pure-Rust candidate; GDAL is everything at a big native cost.

candidates.name: GDAL + gdal crate
candidates.note: Everything raster; per-driver licences; heavy native dependency.

capabilities.title: Snapping, topology validation and vertex editing
capabilities.summary: 1.0's minimal snapping needs nothing beyond geo; these matter at 2.x.

capabilities.title: Model Context Protocol framing, transports and schemas
capabilities.summary: Speak the MCP spec; rmcp (official Rust SDK) is the candidate at mcp-server-permission-model. Weekly releases are the cost. Both repos carry a mid-transition licence text (Apache-2.0 for new work, residual MIT).

candidates.name: rmcp
candidates.note: Candidate; the human decides on the dependency.

capabilities.title: Isolated plugins with a versioned, stable ABI
capabilities.summary: Zed shows ADR-009's split in a shipping product (copyleft host, Apache-2.0 API crate, WIT versioned by directory) but runs extensions in-process, which ADR-009 forbids for proprietary plugins. Own the out-of-process boundary and the ABI versioning.

candidates.name: Zed
candidates.note: since_vX WIT layout and host shims.

decisions_for_human: In-process WASM plugins versus ADR-009's out-of-process rule (human and counsel).

capabilities.title: Spatial indexes for pruning reads, picking or culling
capabilities.summary: Closed by measurement (docs/07, kernel/RESULTS.md): no index pruned IO; layout stays out of the import path. Reopen only by a fresh preregistered gate on (1) a small-viewport-dominant workload, (2) ADR-011's tiled batches removing whole-extent reads, or (3) a demonstrated writer confound.

candidates.name: geo-index
candidates.note: Hilbert/STR sorts and packed index; serves (2) and (3). Its geo feature is geo 0.31.

candidates.name: rstar
candidates.note: Already in the lock via geo; serves (2).

licence_watch.summary: earcut moved from ISC to MIT OR Apache-2.0 (c4e2cdc, 2026-04-25; first release 0.4.10), but still ships LICENSE-ISC for Mapbox-derived code. The engine locks 0.4.5 (ISC). At the next geo bump the label changes; the ISC notice is still owed. DEPENDENCY-LICENSES.md reads labels, so it would miss this.

generateNotice.mjs enumerates only build manifests and DuckDB's tree, so a ported MIT file under frontends/shell/src would be missing from the shipped NOTICE. Before any PORT: a notice route (hash-pinned texts plus an SPDX header), or a fresh write from the algorithm.
package.json says ISC; LICENSE.txt is BSD-3-Clause twice with non-endorsement clauses.
Declares MIT OR Apache-2.0 but ships only an MIT LICENSE.
MCP spec and rmcp: Apache-2.0 for new work, residual MIT for un-consented contributions; mixed notice set.
No LICENSE file; licence only in Cargo.toml files and a README badge that links to another project's LICENSE; vendors Karney's geodesic.c.
Shipping PROJ's proj.db embeds EPSG v13.104, extending the IOGP terms question from two definitions to the dataset.
clipper2-rust's BSL-1.0 is the Boost licence (permissive); a keyword scan for BSL would misfile it as Business Source.
The shell's lockfile carries loader-utils 4.4.4 (transitive), whose RequestScheduler restarts its debounce on every completion; fixed in 4.5.3.
